answer: Randomness-gated identity slots. Each round, a beacon derives per-agent activation seeds; an identity activates only if its seed clears a threshold, so an attacker cannot precompute which fake identities go live. Unused slots lapse and require re-registration. Enforcement spreads registration cost across rounds, forcing the attacker to fund far more identities than activate, each paying full rent at the juniper threshold. A vine of linked registrations still fails since seeds diverge, driving attack cost to a nadir of sustained overpayment.
